agent: effects wave C - the iterating scopes, limit, and the 31 recorded Execute bodies
question: What each iterating effect scope walks, in what order, what it rebinds, how limit filters and how a random_* member is drawn; and whether the 31 recorded effect Executes say what the effect does well enough to rebuild it.

addresses.name: CAnyOwnedEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAnyOwnedEffect::Execute(CAnyOwnedEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **`any_owned = { limit = { ... } effects }`.** 0x5AC6E0 to the one `ret 8` at 0x5AC7FE, fifteen int3 after, then slot 8 at 0x5AC810. Walks `countries[scope->country_id (+0x14)]->OwnedProvinces (CCountry +0xCF0)` - a `CList<int>` of province ids, node `{id, prev, next@+8}` - in list order. **For every member the local scope is re-copied field by field from the scope it was given** (+0x4..+0x44, all of them) and then `province (+0x28)` is set to the member; the **country is kept**. So each province's effects start from the parent's `random_state (+0x8)`: a `random` or `random_list` inside rolls **the same number for every province**, and nothing a member draws is seen by the next or by the parent. The `limit` (the CAndTrigger at +0x20, slot 6 `Evaluate`) is asked against that per-member scope; an absent limit is an empty AND and is true. When it answers 1 the children run with the per-member scope and the second argument passed on. The next node is read **before** the limit and the children run, so a member's effects removing the current province from the list do not break the walk. No guard on the country: country 0 indexes the empty tag's object. The parent scope is never written.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x5AC6E0-0x5AC7FE: `mov ebx,[eax+0xcf0]` at 0x5AC719, the per-iteration copy of [esi+4]..[esi+0x44] into the local at 0x5AC739-0x5AC7AC with `mov [esp+0x40],eax` (local+0x28), `mov ebx,[ebx+8]` at 0x5AC736 before the limit call `call [ [edi+0x20] + 0x18 ]` at 0x5AC7CA, children `call [vft+0x2c]` with `[ebp+0xc]`. Held at slot 11 by CAnyOwnedEffect's table only (vtable.py). Wrong if the copy were made once before the loop, which would show as no [esi+8] read inside it.

addresses.name: CAnyControlledEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAnyControlledEffect::Execute(CAnyControlledEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **`any_controlled`.** 0x5AC9A0 to the one `ret 8` at 0x5ACABE. Byte for byte the shape of CAnyOwnedEffect::Execute with `ControlledProvinces (CCountry +0xD00)` in place of `+0xCF0`: list order, a fresh per-member copy of the given scope (so every member starts from the parent's random_state), `province` set to the member, country kept, limit asked against the member scope, children given the second argument. The next node is read before the member's effects run.

addresses.name: CAnyCountryEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAnyCountryEffect::Execute(CAnyCountryEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **`any_country`, and it visits countries that do not exist.** 0x5AC1F0 to the one `ret 8` at 0x5AC363. Copies the scope **once**, then for `i = 0` while `i < CGameState::GetCountryCount()` (slot 6 of the game state, re-asked every iteration) takes `CCountryDataBase +0x16C [i]` and writes its own `CountryTag (+0xCA4/+0xCA8)` into the copy's `country_tag/country_id`; **`province` is not cleared**, so a province condition or effect inside sees the province the block was entered with. Then the limit is asked against the copy, and the children run only if it answers 1 **and the country's id is not the scope's own** - the scope's country is skipped, after its limit has been evaluated. **Nothing tests existence**: index 0 (the empty tag) and every country that owns nothing are visited unless the limit says `exists = yes` - unlike `random_country`, which drops them. Because the copy is made once, random draws made inside one member's effects (and `ally`/`local_enemy` contexts in the limit) carry on into the next member's; the parent's random_state is never advanced.
addresses.evidence: Listing: CopyConstruct at 0x5AC21C before the loop and nowhere inside it; `call [vft+0x18]` on [0x1A89790] at 0x5AC2A4 each iteration; `mov ecx,[eax+0xca4]; mov esi,[eax+0xca8]` at 0x5AC2F4; limit then `cmp esi,[eax+0x14]` at 0x5AC323. No read of +0xCF8 anywhere in the body (the positive control is CRandomCountryEffect::CollectCandidates, which reads it at 0x5ACF88).

addresses.name: CAnyNeighborCountryEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAnyNeighborCountryEffect::Execute(CAnyNeighborCountryEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **`any_neighbor_country`.** 0x5ABE90 to the one `ret 8` at 0x5ABF2A. Copies the scope once and walks `countries[scope->country_id]->Neighbours (CCountry +0xFD8)` - the 0x14-byte `CCountryList` nodes `{tag, id, prev@+8, next@+0xC}` - in list order, writing each tag into the copy's country; `province` is **not** cleared. addresses.name: CAnyNeighborProvinceEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAnyNeighborProvinceEffect::Execute(CAnyNeighborProvinceEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **`any_neighbor_province`.** 0x5AB590 to the `ret 8` at 0x5AB7AD, and slot 8 begins at 0x5AB7B0 on the very next byte (no padding - trap 2; functionStart answers 0x5AB590 for anything in slot 8's first bytes). Walks the edge records of the scope province - `provinces[scope->province (+0x28)]->path_node_ptr (+0xD4)`, `edges_begin/edges_end (CProvinceTemplate +0x90/+0x94)`, 0x14 bytes each, far province at edge+4 - in edge order, and **skips any neighbour whose `owner_id (+0x330)` is 0**, so sea zones and unowned land are never visited. addresses.name: CRandomCountryEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CRandomCountryEffect::Execute(CRandomCountryEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **`random_country`.** 0x5ACC60 to the `ret 8` at 0x5ACD1C; one int3, then slot 8 at 0x5ACD20. First CRandomCountryEffect::CollectCandidates (0x5ACE50) rebuilds the candidate list at `+0x60` - existing countries only, never the scope's own, limit applied - so **the limit filters before the draw**. If the count (+0x68) is 0 nothing happens and **the scope's random state is not touched**. Otherwise two steps of the LCG `s = s*0x343FD + 0x269EC3` on `scope->random_state (+0x8)`, **written back into the given scope**, `r = ((s1>>16)&0x7FFF) * ((s2>>16)&0x7FFF)` (a non-negative product below 2^30), `index = r % count` (`cdq; idiv`), and the list is walked `index` nodes from its head. A copy of the scope is made **after** the write-back, its country set to the chosen tag, province left alone, and the children run against it with the second argument passed on. One draw per execution; whatever the children draw stays in the copy.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x5ACC73 `call 0x9ACE50` (VA), `cmp [ebx+0x68],0; jle`, LCG at 0x5ACC82-0x5ACC9D with `mov [edi+8],eax`, CopyConstruct at 0x5ACCC2, `idiv dword [esp+0x14]` at 0x5ACCD0, walk `mov eax,[eax+0xc]`, tag/id into local+0x10/+0x14.

addresses.name: EventRandom_NextProduct
addresses.signature: int __stdcall EventRandom_NextProduct(unsigned int* state@EDX) @EAX
addresses.comment: **The event scope's random draw, as a function.** Thirteen instructions, bare `ret` at 0x6A2EC0. `s1 = *state * 0x343FD + 0x269EC3; s2 = s1 * 0x343FD + 0x269EC3; *state = s2; return ((s2 >> 16) & 0x7FFF) * ((s1 >> 16) & 0x7FFF)` - MSVC's `rand` recurrence stepped twice, the two 15-bit outputs multiplied, so the answer is in [0, 0x3FFF0001] and never negative. Every caller reduces it the same way, `cdq; idiv count` - **index = product % count** - and passes `&scope->random_state (+0x8)`: CEventScope::MakeScope's `ally`/`local_enemy` arms (0x5C1F17), CReleaseVassalEffect::ResolveTarget (0x5AF6F8) and CSplitTroopsEffect::Execute (0x5BB595, `% 100`). The iterating effects, CRandomEffect, CRandomListEffect and CCountryEventEffect inline the same two steps instead of calling it. ECX is not read.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x6A2E90-0x6A2EC0 (decoded at VA 0xAA2E90); findRefs --callers gives exactly three direct calls, 0x9AF6F8, 0x9BB595, 0x9C1F17 (VAs). MakeScope's reduction at 0x5C1F1C-0x5C1F1D is `cdq; idiv ebx`. Wrong if a caller masked or shifted the product before reducing it.

addresses.name: CAnyNearbyProvinceEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAnyNearbyProvinceEffect::Execute(CAnyNearbyProvinceEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **`any_nearby_province = { distance = N limit = { ... } effects }`, a province scope.** 0x5ABA30 to the one `ret 8` at 0x5ABBF2. Copies the scope once. Takes the scope's province (+0x28), its **controller** (`+0x338`), and walks `countries[controller]->ControlledProvinces (CCountry +0xD00)` in list order - so the scope never leaves the controller's land, and **the scope province itself is a member** (distance 0). For each it computes `dx, dy` between the two provinces' centres (`g_CMap +0x2A60` templates, x at +0x2C, y at +0x30), wraps `|dx|` against the world width at `g_CMap +0x2A74` when it exceeds half of it, and keeps the province when **`16 * (dx*dx + dy*dy) <= distance*distance`** - i.e. `4 * sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2) <= distance`, so `distance` is in quarters of a map pixel, the game's kilometres. Distance is tested before the limit; the limit is then asked against the copy with the member as its province (country kept), and the children run with the second argument passed on. Random state carries across members. **Corrected 2026-10-12: the record said `dx*dx + dy*dy <= distance*distance`, which drops the `shl edi, 4` at 0x5ABB8D.** First read in reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md; signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.comment: **Slot 11, what the `practical` effect does.** 0x5BDCF0 to the one `ret 8` at 0x5BDDA3. Returns at once unless the scope carries a country (`scope->country_id != 0`). Takes the technology category from the effect's +0x20, its index from CTechnologyCategory +0x5C, and the country's level for it from own_ability (CCountry +0x698). **Where that category has a technology-sharing partner** - CCountry +0x6A8, a CCountryTag per category - it reads the partner's level too and takes whichever is higher as the base. Then it adds the effect's `value` (+0x24, fixed point) and stores the result through CCountry::SetTechAbility (0xE03C0), which floors at 0 and caps at MAX_TECH_ABILITY. **It is not restricted to practicals**: the category map it resolves against holds theories too and a country keeps one own_ability array for both, so `technology_group = infantry_theory` works and is the only way a script can move a theory - CEffect::LoadKey has no `theory` keyword. CCountry::LoadKey's own handling of a `*_theory` or `*_practical` key in a history file (rva 0xCF2F3) is the same lookup and the same array, assigning rather than adding. **It never runs its child effects**: CPracticalEffect::LoadKey hands unknown keys to CEffect::LoadKey, so effects written inside a `practical` block are parsed into its child list and then ignored - there is no walk of `+0x8` and no slot-11 dispatch anywhere in the body. A null category (+0x20) is dereferenced without a test. First read in reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md; signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md).

addresses.comment: `<sub-unit type> = <where>`. Province: `g_CMap->provinces[+0x20 / 1000]`, or THIS scope's province (use_this), THIS scope's FROM province (use_from), or the scope's own province (use_current). Owner: the scope country, or the province's **controller** with `current`. Unless the definition is the HQ brigade, it picks the owner's unit in the province with fewer than four regiments, of the right arm (land/air/naval by the definition's flags), **whose first regiment is not an HQ**, preferring the emptiest (`(4 - count) * 10`, strictly greater, so the first of equals wins); an HQ brigade always gets a unit of its own. Then RebuildAvatar, EnterProvince and CCombatManager::CheckForCombat. So a scripted brigade arrives at **half strength and half organisation**.

addresses.name: CContextEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CContextEffect::Execute(CContextEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **Slot 11, and the effect side of scoping narrows exactly as the trigger side does.** 0x59E2B0 to the one `ret 8` at 0x59E2FB, 0x4C bytes, two int3 then CContextEffect::GetText at 0x59E300. It builds a 0x48-byte CEventScope on its own stack, calls `CEventScope::MakeScope(scope, this->spec (+0x20), &out)` - the same already-recorded function (0x5C1C10) CContextTrigger uses, which builds the answer in a local copy of the receiver, overwrites only country and/or province, and writes `out` once at an exit - tests `out.resolved (+0x3C)`, and only then walks its children dispatching slot 11 on each with `&out`. So `GER = { ... }` or `owner = { ... }` in an effect block **narrows the scope it was given rather than building a new one**, and the ten context tokens and their meanings are the ones FINDINGS-triggereval.md read. Two differences from the trigger side worth having: an unresolvable context here is a **silent no-op** rather than a false, so the rest of the block still runs; and the children are passed a literal **0** as the second argument, not this effect's own. **Randomness**: the children run against the copy, so a `random` inside does not advance the enclosing block's state; but the `ally` and `local_enemy` forms draw through EventRandom_NextProduct on the **enclosing** scope's random_state (FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md section 13), so resolving them does. 10,686 live instances.

structs.evidence: operator new(0x70) at VA 0x99A765 before the vftable write at VA 0x99A78E; RTTI base CMultipleTargetEffect.

structs.name: CRandomEmptyNeighborProvinceEffect
structs.comment: `random_empty_neighbor_province`. Candidate list of province ids at +0x60.
structs.evidence: operator new(0x70) at VA 0x99AD61 before the vftable write at VA 0x99AD8A; RTTI base CMultipleTargetEffect.

structs.name: CAnyNearbyProvinceEffect
structs.comment: `any_nearby_province`. Its own data is `distance` at +0x60; its own LoadKey (rva 0x5ABC00) reads it.
structs.evidence: operator new(0x64) at VA 0x99B10F before the vftable write at VA 0x99B138; RTTI base CMultipleTargetEffect.

struct_fields.name: candidates
struct_fields.comment: The countries the next draw chooses among: existing, not the scope's own, passing the limit, in database order. Rebuilt from nothing by CRandomCountryEffect::CollectCandidates on every Execute and every tooltip; first/last/count at +0x60/+0x64/+0x68.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x5ACE92-0x5ACE98 zero +0x60/+0x64/+0x68; append writes 0x14-byte nodes {tag, id, prev, next@+0xC}; Execute reads +0x68 as the count and walks from +0x60 on node+0xC.

struct_fields.name: candidates
struct_fields.comment: Province ids the next draw chooses among, rebuilt by CRandomOwnedEffect::CollectCandidates.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x5AD24D-0x5AD253 zero +0x60/+0x64/+0x68; 0x10-byte nodes {id, prev, next@+8}; Execute walks node+8.

struct_fields.name: candidates
struct_fields.comment: Neighbouring province ids with an owner that pass the limit, rebuilt by CRandomNeighborProvinceEffect::CollectCandidates.
struct_fields.evidence: The builder zeroes +0x60/+0x64/+0x68 and appends 0x10-byte nodes; Execute reads +0x68 and walks node+8.

struct_fields.name: candidates
struct_fields.comment: Neighbouring unowned land province ids that pass the limit, rebuilt by CRandomEmptyNeighborProvinceEffect::CollectCandidates.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x5AE1A5-0x5AE1AB zero +0x60/+0x64/+0x68; Execute reads +0x68 and walks node+8 from +0x60.

struct_fields.name: distance
struct_fields.comment: `distance = N`, a plain integer (sscanf %i, no thousandths) in quarters of a map pixel: a province is near when 16 * (dx^2 + dy^2) <= distance^2 between the two centres.
struct_fields.evidence: CAnyNearbyProvinceEffect::LoadKey writes it (record); Execute reads `mov ecx,[edi+0x60]; imul ecx,ecx` at 0x5ABAF8-0x5ABB01.
